8.3 Reproduction order and offline, local, and hosted dependencies

tbl. 21 lists the reproduction path from the project root. Set and export TEMPLATE_REPO_ROOT to the existing template checkout’s path before running the table. The render and validation commands use that variable to change directory in a subshell. Core level verdicts are independent of the model server. Re-measuring the external reference frame of sec. 13, including the stipulated controls, uses the network claim phase and requires a local Ollama server with all registered probes available and, for the two hosted scored-call recorders, an exported OPENROUTER_API_KEY. A missing probe or key refuses the comparison rather than silently shrinking its declared family. Environment installation and count regeneration from upstream sources may also require downloads. The committed counts support offline core evaluation.

That network phase stores calls individually, keyed by the request, endpoint, protocol and transport-specific identity. Local Ollama calls require a server-supplied content digest or a validated content blob in a stable build manifest. Hosted OpenRouter calls instead hash requested and returned model slugs; a hash of a logical slug is not a hash of serving weights. Capped hosted runs additionally bind the selected provider and price constraints in both the exact cached payload and the run receipt, retaining raw server response and usage evidence. This documents the serving route and observed response, while provider-side weight immutability remains unverified. The synthetic and in-context recorders retain registered probe tags as run labels, but their scored calls use the hosted model named in the receipt, not distinct local weights. Replay is protocol-specific. The external benchmark can reuse eligible ordinary calls, but its repeat-agreement trials make both requests fresh. Every scored synthetic and in-context call is fresh on a publication run. The drift recorder pairs authenticated stored log-probability replies with fresh uncached observations. Re-running the phase is therefore a new measurement and can change scientific values.

The external, synthetic, and in-context recorders namespace every fresh scored call with a UTC run scope, the registered probe tag, and that call’s own position slot — every scored call’s namespace is unique within its run, because the hosted transport’s replies are not assumed deterministic — preserving older records without overwriting them. The in-context recorder authenticates the synthetic producer’s stored zero-shot replies under that producer’s scope before making its own scored calls. The drift recorder instead binds its sampled stored records and new observation pairs directly. Receipts record hit, miss, and fresh-call accounting as execution evidence; their validator reconstructs the claims from the exact declared records and rejects missing, extra, or inconsistent evidence. Source and vendored-input manifests must remain unchanged throughout recording.

Separately, the external recorder’s --verify-cache audit re-measures a stratified sample, requires exact answer strings, and compares log-probability candidates at aligned emitted positions under the frozen tolerance before writing claims. Distribution-bearing rows must retain their emitted-token identity and shared candidates; the audit does not flatten candidates across different output contexts. Its strata cross registered probes with ordinary and answer-distribution requests. This compares current replies with the sampled stored replies; it establishes neither stability of every cached call nor a guarantee about future server behavior.

The ordinary offline inventory is the dynamically discovered scripts/record_*_claims.py set. scripts/record_confirmatory_replication.py deliberately sits outside it: decision 111’s sentinel records that the held-back population has been spent and refuses another scoring run. Ordinary reproduction preserves that record. By contrast, scripts/record_confirmatory_stage6_clustered_claims.py belongs to core: decision 115 permits deterministic replay of its separately specified estimand on the already-spent population with frozen development fits. Its status remains descriptive; replay supplies no new held-back replication.

Table 21: The complete reproduction path. Stop on any unexpected nonzero command; later rows do not repair an earlier failure. The Lean mutation row uses the diagnostic-validating pytest control; a raw shell negation would also accept an unrelated path, import, parse, or toolchain error and is not evidence that Lean rejected the intended mutations. scripts/audit_gates.py exits non-zero if an ordinary implemented gate is not bracketed or if a model contradicts its recorded outcome, so it is a check rather than a report. It audits both clause arms on every run and writes the retained ablation to its own export, output/reports/gate_audit_ablation.json, so the canonical export keeps exactly the registered gate inventory and no more. The ablation is the explicit ABOVE_REFERENCE exception: a mixture pass, a fitted privileged reference crossing the bar, or a paired whole-document cluster-bootstrap interval that moves off zero is a changed finding and trips the exit code; its current status is non-passing with unresolved gain. The canonical Stage 5 row declares no exception and is held to the ordinary rule, a bracketed placement and a passing outcome (sec. 4.2).

Generated prerequisites must be current before the full suite or release profile starts: those tests consume figure and cover outputs, local web artifacts, both gate-audit reports, and Stage 04 provenance. Hydrated repository documentation is also generated and checked before rendering. The release profile subsequently repairs individual HTML references from the actual combined index and performs strict complete HTML checks before Stage 04 binds final provenance. It regenerates and checks these outputs. The gate-audit and claims-discipline rows of tbl. 21 are the minimum pair a reader should run. scripts/audit_gates.py re-derives the gate classification from measured baselines and ceilings rather than from anything recorded, so it would catch a threshold that had drifted back into vacuity. tests/test_claims_discipline.py scans the real repository tree rather than a fixture, which is what makes it a statement about the shipped artifact (sec. 4.11). Where a reproducibility checklist such as (Pineau et al. 2021) asks an author to self-report a study’s degrees of freedom, this repository’s gate audit and claims-discipline scan check the corresponding properties mechanically against the shipped tree on every run, rather than once at submission time.

8.4 Interactive inspection and the reply-generation boundary

The local dashboard exposes input controls and a temporal trajectory beside a chat demonstration (fig. 27). Its input-analysis views and generated reply have different computational scopes: the reply follows the L3-to-L1g policy path described in sec. 4.9. The upper-level input posteriors do not constitute an end-to-end reply-generation cascade. The matrix explorer provides a separate inspection surface. These interfaces support inspection; they do not add an evaluation population to the results.

8.5 Variable injection and source provenance

All 2577 claims live in data/claims.json, each recorded by the run that produced it with its run_id and source location. src/ailm/manuscript_variables/ supplies the double-brace token map this manuscript is written against. Recorded-value tokens follow a mechanical rule: the token is the ledger label uppercased, so stage1_letter_perplexity becomes STAGE1_LETTER_PERPLEXITY. Provenance companions are generated alongside each value, so a claim’s originating run is available without a separate lookup. Other tokens are explicitly derived expressions or configuration and metadata values; they do not acquire ledger entries merely by appearing in the map.

The failure behavior is the point. A required claim absent from the ledger raises MissingClaimError and the render stops; it does not emit a plausible default and does not leave an unresolved marker in the output, because an unresolved token in a rendered PDF reads as a fabricated result. tests/test_manuscript_variables.py tests that failure path claim by claim, deleting each required label in turn and requiring the error to name it. The consequence for a reader is narrow but real: each ledger-backed value in sec. 5 can be traced to its entry and owning recorder; derived values require the additional calculation in the token writer. The refusal protects required recorded inputs. It does not prove the measurements correct or make arbitrary hand-written numerals impossible.

A concrete trace starts at tbl. 9, which prints the letter-level perplexity as the token STAGE1_LETTER_PERPLEXITY. Lowercasing gives the ledger label stage1_letter_perplexity; its companions resolve to run stage1_letter_gate and source scripts/record_stage1_claims.py. Running that recorder, .venv/bin/python scripts/record_stage1_claims.py, re-records the entry; .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_stage1_gate.py -v recomputes the same perplexity from the vendored counts and re-applies the declared bar; and .venv/bin/python scripts/audit_gates.py re-derives the verdict that bar is judged under. The first two steps of that walk — token to label, label to run and source — are mechanical and hold for every one of the 2577 claims. Only the last step is claim-specific, and it is not guesswork either: the source field names the script that recorded the number. tbl. 21 identifies the ordinary recorder phases; the one-shot replication is retained under its separate protocol above.

Selected mathematical claims are stated and proved in Lean 4 under formal/: the gate taxonomy of eq. 10 and eq. 12, the pre-registered sweep-shape predicates of sec. 4.10, both halves of eq. 6, and the Bonferroni arithmetic behind tbl. 36. The layer ships 149 named theorems and 34 witness examples with a recorded formal_sorry_free verdict of true, and it cannot drift from the recorded measurements: the one ledger-facing module is generated from data/claims.json, byte-identity-checked on regeneration, and every ledger-facing theorem that fixes a threshold closes by decide, so a re-record that moves a measured value across a declared threshold stops the corresponding proof from compiling. What the layer does not establish — that any recorded number is correct — and the rest of its deliberate scope boundaries are set out in sec. 14.

8.6 Deterministic build epoch and figures

This document was rendered at 2026-10-27T02:45:22Z from version 1.0.0. The timestamp honors SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH; when it is omitted, the manuscript orchestrator derives the epoch of the last audited commit that touched an input outside the regenerable output/ tree, so the build stamp remains reproducible along with everything else and a commit that only refreshes rendered output does not move it. Figures are written deterministically by src/ailm/figures/ with fixed layout and recorded inputs. Where a figure validates a bootstrap statistic, it uses the registered seed. Numeric content is drawn from the same recorded values as the prose. Sharing that source removes a separate transcription step; correct token selection, current generation, and rendered figure/table agreement still require their own checks.

One caveat on exact equality: pymdp computes in float32 under JAX, so analytic anchors are compared with recorder- or test-owned tolerances rather than exact equality. A uniform transition over 39 phones measures marginally below 39, not exactly it. That float32 premise is recorded, not assumed: jax_enable_x64 is recorded as false, preserving the default float32 path used by the shipped pymdp agents. The Stage 0 recorder pins the live flag at record time (env_jax_enable_x64, alongside the JAX, jaxlib, and pymdp versions and the platform) and refuses to record with JAX’s 64-bit mode enabled, since a flipped flag would change the numeric story, not merely the rendering. tests/test_pymdp_smoke.py asserts the recorded value still matches the live interpreter after importing the pymdp path, so the recorded premise cannot silently outlive the environment it describes. Reproducing the figures to the byte requires the same matplotlib and font stack; reproducing the numbers requires only the pinned environment.

8.7 Availability and retained upstream licenses

AILM’s own code (src/, scripts/, tests/, formal/, and gnn/) is licensed MIT; the manuscript, documentation, figures, and other authored data are licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. The vendored count artifacts keep their own, narrower upstream terms, which neither AILM license relicenses: the Brown-derived counts carry NLTK’s non-commercial package terms, the Czech-PDTC artifact is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, the English EWT artifacts are CC BY-SA 4.0, and the CMUdict counts retain the upstream BSD-2-Clause notice. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md inventories each component with its transformation, and LICENSE states the commercial-use boundary the two non-commercial artifacts impose on the distributed wheel.

The recorded environment names an arm64 workstation (macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit) and the pinned JAX precision setting. The CUDA extra is an untested install path. These fields do not record device placement for each computation and do not establish CPU-only execution of the separate Ollama model server. No wall-clock performance claim is made here.

The work has a single author, who wrote every gate the audit reports on and every control that tests it. The external scrutiny to date is the audit and cross-vendor model reviews recorded in the decisions log, which the author commissioned and answered; no independent reproduction of the checkout is recorded in this evidence.

The work received no funding: there are no grants and no external funding of any kind. The author has no competing interests to declare.

sec. 6.1 states what that single-author position means for the gate-audit method’s own evidence.

9 Established Findings and the Next Independent Tests

AILM now combines explicit GNN-declared components with a live conditional message schedule. The connected GUM result, the historical component experiments and the gate-audit method support different conclusions and retain their own populations, comparators and limitations.

The six modeled levels are built and their outcomes recorded; one of the six verdicts is qualified. The clause level clears a gate that was registered before its artifact existed, on an observation alphabet widened past the case roles, and its privileged-label gain resolves away from zero under a paired whole-document bootstrap. That gate is a development-session specification and has no held-back replication, because the held-back partition was already spent. The case-only clause model it displaced is retained as an ablation: its gate is non-passing, its privileged-label gain is unresolved on both reported scales under the same bootstrap, and its detectability control recovers a larger planted effect but supplies no equivalence claim (decision 83). The document-position (tercile) level — narrative in code — has a positive point estimate in a direction timestamped before its measurement, but its document-clustered primary interval spans zero and is non-confirmatory (decisions 25–26). The same estimand, registered separately under decision 115 and carried to the held-back split, gives 0.008288 nats with an interval that excludes zero at the development coverage and spans zero at the family-corrected one, on a population whose own resolution, 0.005726 nats, is coarser than the development-sized effect (sec. 5.8.2); the development result is not retracted by it. The level’s sentence-sign statistic is secondary and nominally positive; it crosses neither the fixed Bonferroni threshold nor its Holm step-down threshold, the fixed threshold being the one 7 of 16 declared tests cross. sec. 5 holds the letter and phoneme measurements and points to where each later level’s measurements are recorded. All level builders produce ordinary pymdp agents, but among the historical stage scores only L1’s headline filters live; the later levels’ exact or NumPy score paths and the live-Agent checks that license them are inventoried in tbl. 3 and sec. 4.11. Two of those checks are exhaustive: L5 uses an exact closed-form mixture with a live-Agent posterior-agreement check on the full held-out set that is not score equivalence, and L4 uses a NumPy filter that the live Agent reproduces at every held-out position.

The historical stack first established representational hierarchy: L2B infers over a variable L1 represents, observing the alphabet L1’s states are drawn from. The historical standalone decoders exchange no beliefs. The seven registered receiver interventions are built on that composition: five measured separately, the case-word bridge measured as an exploratory prior-only sweep on the development population, and its privileged-oracle diagnostic the one registered seam that records no estimand. The measured ones disagree in sign. The L3→L2B lexical channel and L1→L2B coupling enter the same letter-to-phone receiver but differ in sender: the lexical channel helps (+3.333 pts at p = 3.756e-102), the coupling harms (moving accuracy -0.2639 pts at p = 1.547e-06). L3→L1g, the lexicon-to-letter preference used by the recorded generation run, helps without a paired significance test behind it. The independent L6→L5 and privileged punctuation-type-oracle→L3 interventions are less clean and stay on the record as such. L6→L5 moves the case-only clause model’s D prior against a tercile-scrambled control, in a receiver whose privileged-label gain is unresolved. The independent oracle→L3 word-prior intervention is a corrected helpful result on both directional summaries that falsified its predicted harm (sec. 4.10). It is not evidence about an L5 output channel. These experiments were not executed as a connected cascade. The subsequent connected runtime executes explicit conditional messages and live next-word policy selection. Its locally frozen GUM comparison spans 22 previously unexamined documents after excluding 8 development documents. The mean paired normalized-character log-loss gain is 0.4420177562251402 nats with interval [0.42010385279024465, 0.46325671494396264], indicating lower integrated loss. Full-stream word loss remains infinite because out-of-vocabulary tokens receive zero word probability. These are results for a fixed conditional schedule and normalization, not a globally exact joint posterior or external replication (sec. 5.1).

Comprehension filtering alone does not distinguish the system from classical Bayesian state estimation. Every modeled level has a flat C and a single action in comprehension, so no policy is scored and no expected free energy is computed. L1’s headline and the bounded L2 verification paths execute live filtering; that recursion is the forward algorithm of a hidden Markov model, while the L2 full-set and later headline scores use the exact or NumPy paths just enumerated. This is precisely what lets a plain-NumPy HMM serve as the implementation-independent reference decoder at the checked levels (sec. 7). The additional policy-selection mechanism is exercised in generation, where the letter transition is made controllable and the lexicon supplies the only non-flat preference vector in the system, so the emitted symbol is selected by minimizing expected free energy over policies (sec. 4.9). Even that one place is narrower than it sounds, and saying so is a result rather than a concession: because the controllable transition is deterministic, the information-gain term is identically zero and policy selection reduces analytically to a preference-weighted softmax over the habit (eq. 17). The measurement is reported with a control that restores the term to its analytic ceiling, so the claim is that the formalism contributes nothing beyond that softmax here, not that it could not elsewhere. A transition that is both stochastic and action-dependent would put the term back and let it bear on the choice; the uniform-transition control fixes the ceiling such a design works within, and the word-state construction of sec. 4.9 shows that uncertainty without action-dependence buys nothing. The budgeted-attention arm (sec. 6.1) already measures the case where that term is the whole policy. The gate-audit findings that follow concern these filtering models and the thresholds written for them; they are not a verdict on active inference as a general framework.

The more transferable results are the gate-audit method and the negative findings. A load-bearing modeling decision, which slot the learned matrix occupies, was wrong in a way the library could not detect. pymdp validates more than normalization: it checks array shapes against declared factor dependencies, index bounds, and control consistency. What no structural check reaches is semantics. A column-stochastic bigram is column-stochastic whichever slot it occupies, and nothing in the library knows whether an axis was intended to mean next given current or its transpose. The wrong wiring was not loudly broken but quietly anti-informative, and it slipped under a threshold that had never been checked against either a trivial baseline or an achievable ceiling. Then the same class of oversight produced two opposite gate defects: one threshold no correct implementation could ever reach, one that a lookup table already cleared. The detection method is the same in both directions, and it is cheap: measure what a model doing none of the work scores, measure what the data allows, and accept a threshold only when the first fails it and the second clears it.

That check is expected to generalize past this project and past active inference, a working hypothesis in the sense of sec. 2: its evidence is every declared gate of one repository, written and audited by one author, and nothing outside it has yet been tested. It would apply to any staged or gated build whose progress is defined by a numeric criterion: accuracy floors in a test suite, latency budgets, coverage thresholds, benchmark targets in a research program. The taxonomy of sec. 4.2 needs only three measured quantities, two of which can usually be obtained before the system exists, and the checklist there is written to be run before the build rather than after the result. scripts/audit_gates.py is what makes it a re-runnable artifact instead of something someone happened to do twice; the same shape would fit any repository with declared thresholds.

The check was then turned on a threshold of our own, which is the harder half of the same lesson. The benchmark originally refused to report a calibration number when too little of a model’s reported distribution was observed, and that floor was declared on an argument rather than measured. Measuring where it belongs put it at 1.9826100924184078 times the declared value, and at a mass the serving interface cannot supply for 0.395 of positions: the floor was not conservative, and no reachable gate of that shape would be (sec. 13). The instructive part is how nearly the measurement endorsed the wrong answer. Both metrics’ rule disagreement crosses zero once, essentially at the declared floor, while the two reconstructions are still far apart; a locator that took the first crossing would have confirmed 0.5 by a coincidence of opposite biases. A threshold that survives its own audit is not thereby correct, and the audit needs its own negative control.

One reporting change follows from the same discipline. Every interval-spanning paired result in this project is stated as an interval rather than as an absence, because “no effect was found” is weaker than the data support and hides the distinction that matters: no near-null arm in the plotted paired-bound roster produced enough discordant pairs to support an equivalence claim, so each bounds its effect and says nothing about absence (sec. 15.3). The one arm that once did, the lexical channel at its highest tested weight, became a decided effect when its backoff defect was corrected (decision 110), and the roster now holds bounds only. A bounded effect and an unresolved one can read alike in a table; separating them is the reporting result.

The project’s other negative result is about its own headline architecture. An inter-level message, L1’s predictive over letters folded into L2B’s observation likelihood, was built rather than assumed, and it moved accuracy by -0.2639 points against the uncoupled decode, a loss significant at paired McNemar p = 1.547e-06. The channel works; it simply carries nothing L2B does not already observe. Reporting that is the point: the mechanism had been asserted in this project’s own documentation before anyone measured it, which is the same failure as an unfalsified threshold, one layer up. By contrast, the L3→L2B lexical channel was prospectively specified in the same development session, built, and measured as helpful (3.333 pts), so the novel-information criterion (decisions 18–19) is falsifiable, and on that pair — same receiving level, opposite senders — its prediction matched the development-population result. Its next test went the other way. The privileged punctuation-type-oracle→L3 word-prior intervention, which the criterion itself named as its cheapest falsification and predicted would harm, instead moved the word prior’s held-out perplexity slightly in the helpful direction throughout the tested positive grid; the best tested weight is its high endpoint, not a located optimum (3.268023 → 3.263007, decision 27 and sec. 5.10.3); the token-direction tally agrees, with 51,364 improved against 22,649 made less probable. The predicted harm was not supported, so the criterion’s first clause is qualified on that channel. One prospectively specified supporting result and one corrected result that falsifies the criterion’s prediction leave a criterion under test, not an established one.

Three subsidiary lessons carried real cost here. A reproducible evaluation subsample is not a representative one, and an unbiased subsample of the same size can be too small to establish the effect it correctly measures. The resolution was to remove the constraint that forced subsampling: require an implementation-independent oracle and the pymdp decoder to agree on the bounded comparison subset (0 disagreements), then compute full-set statistics. A verification gate that runs only on synthetic fixtures constrains nothing about the shipped artifact: the claims scanner had never been pointed at real prose, and an unbacked claim sat in the repository’s own README for an entire stage while every test passed. A failure signature that catches the mis-wirings you thought of is necessary but not sufficient: an emission normalized along the wrong axis cleared the baseline comparison while being wrong, and only a column-sum invariant and numerical agreement with the oracle pinned it down.

The staged-gate method’s own description was inaccurate, which is why sec. 2 states the qualification alongside the claim-strength labels rather than leaving it to this section. The original Stage 1–4 gates were restated after those levels had been built or measured because their thresholds were vacuous, unreachable, or named the wrong population (tbl. 22, tbl. 27). Later declarations were also re-scoped during audit. Stage 6’s direction was registered before its held-out measurement, but the development population and analysis family were reused and its clustered primary remains non-confirmatory. The repaired gates and controls are more rigorous, but they do not turn the historical process into sequential validation, and no multiplicity correction repairs population reuse. A rerun of the frozen family against a population never inspected while the gates were written was pre-registered, executed to its first data touch, and retired by exhaustion for the external_lexicon members (decision 91); the ud_ewt_test members were then scored exactly once against the held-back EWT test split under decision 111 (sec. 10.6): two clear the frozen per-test bar in their recorded direction, two yield no discordant pair, and the other twelve members of the family remain development-population inference. The supplements that follow — the gate-audit trails and the confirmatory replication, the channel factorial, operation and byte counts, the registered external probes read as a reference frame rather than a competitiveness claim, the machine-checked Lean layer, and the statistical apparatus the paired results rest on (sec. 10, sec. 11, sec. 12, sec. 13, sec. 14, sec. 15) — carry the detail behind the claims and qualifications stated here. Naming the defect is not the same as fixing it: the same honesty the method claims for its measurements is owed for its own process.

What travels beyond this one repository is the pair the introduction opened with: an explicit discrete generative language system whose probabilities, preferences, habits and policy precision are inspectable, and a gate-audit-and-claims-ledger method for holding a staged build to its own thresholds. Neither depends on active inference to be useful, and neither depends on this corpus, this language, or this author’s own gates having been the ones checked. The next test of either is a build this project did not run: a second staged system, audited by someone other than its builder.

What comes after this paper follows the same three commitments the abstract opens with — a generative model declared in Generalized Notation Notation, an Active Inference formalism that turns that declaration into filtering and policy selection, and a grain of linguistic description the declaration is built along — rather than abandoning any of them for scale. That combination is what makes the open work in sec. 6.4 proposable in the terms this paper already uses: a new level, a new language, or a new cross-implementation render is another GNN declaration and another conformance check, not a different kind of artifact; a globally normalized hierarchy would require a new joint specification and fresh comparisons beyond the conditional connected runtime measured here; and a composition with a large language model, in either direction, is answerable to the same discipline that kept this project’s own fitted-probe proposal from certifying its own circularity. None of that is claimed to have happened. It is what the method this paper reports is for.

10 Supplement A: Gate Audits, Mutation Controls, and Held-Back Replication

sec. 4.2 states the typed gate taxonomy and how a threshold is placed and checked; the verdicts that taxonomy produces are reported with each level’s results in sec. 5. This supplement is the trail behind those verdicts: the re-runnable audit script that classifies every declared threshold, the pre-build checklist the audit experience distilled, the defect findings worked through stage by stage, the Level 3 mis-wiring catalog with the scaling ladder behind it, and the per-member detail of the confirmatory replication on the held-back split.

It sits here rather than in the main text because the reader who wants the verdicts needs a paragraph, and the reader who wants to re-derive them needs the trails. The verdicts stay in sec. 4.2 and sec. 5; the script’s exit conditions, the worked defects, the catalogs, and the replication detail are here. Every number in both places resolves to the same ledger entry.

10.1 Declared-threshold defects and gate audits

10.1.1 Stage 1: the declared threshold sat beyond the information-theoretic ceiling

The Stage 1 gate was declared as >=2 nats above uniform. The declaration is information-theoretic, so it can be checked against the data before any model exists, and doing so takes one pass over the training counts. The conditional entropy \(H_{\text{train}}(X_t \mid X_{t-1})\) of the Brown bigram distribution caps the gain any order-1 letter model can realize over uniform on that distribution at 1.0262 nats. The declared target exceeds that ceiling by a factor of 1.95. By eq. 12 the verdict is UNREACHABLE.

The population qualifier is not a hedge, and dropping it would contradict sec. 3. What that sentence establishes is that the fitting distribution contains barely more than half the first-order information the gate demands, so no amount of better smoothing or better implementation supplies the shortfall from the data the model was given. What it does not establish is anything about the held-out passage: eq. 8 bounds order-1 log loss under \(p_{\text{train}}\) and not under the evaluation sample, whose own first-order optimum can sit either side of it.

The evaluation population is not a second corpus sample. It is the AILM-curated normalized composite of an AILM-authored rhyming sentence, traditional English tongue twisters and nursery verse, and a pangram: a short normalized passage repeated 3 times. The complete UTF-8 protocol string is 1323 bytes, identified as ailm-stage1-letter-evaluation-v1 with SHA-256 prefix 513f73d02c22; its terms are CC BY-SA 4.0 for the AILM selection and normalization; cited source phrases are public domain in the United States. Repetition increases the scoring denominator but does not create independent linguistic material, so this passage supports a deterministic protocol check, not a representative-English claim.

The gap that leaves is worth closing rather than conceding, because the same computation performed on the right population closes it exactly. On the transition positions, cross-entropy under empirical bigram distribution \(q\) decomposes as eq. 20:

\[\mathbb{E}_q\!\left[-\log p(X_t \mid X_{t-1})\right] \;=\; H_q(X_t \mid X_{t-1}) \;+\; \sum_{a} q(a)\,\mathrm{KL}\!\left(q(\cdot \mid a) \,\|\, p(\cdot \mid a)\right),\qquad{(20)}\]

and the second term is non-negative for every order-1 conditional \(p\). The gate, however, scores all \(T\) characters: the first is predicted from the fixed uniform \(D\), and only the remaining \(T-1\) are transitions. Its exact lower bound on the same all-position mean as compute_perplexity is therefore

\[H^{*}_{\mathrm{all}} = \frac{\log |\mathcal{A}| + (T-1)H_q(X_t\mid X_{t-1})}{T}.\qquad{(21)}\]

For this fixture, 1.7893 nats over 1322 transitions plus that initial prediction yields 1.7906 nats over all 1323 scored positions. That all-position quantity — not the transition-only entropy — is the exact lower bound on what any model with this fixed uniform start and first-order conditional can score. It caps the gain available over uniform at 1.6106 nats, still short of the 2-nat target. The declared gate is unreachable on the evaluation population as well as on the training one, and now as a theorem rather than as a hope.

The estimate’s finite-sample bias runs the safe way, which is why so few transitions can carry the argument. The plug-in estimator of an entropy is biased downward in the undersampled regime, by an amount that grows with the number of cells relative to the sample (Miller 1955; Paninski 2003); here that is 1322 transitions over an alphabet admitting \(30 \times 30\) bigrams. A smaller entropy means a larger apparent gain, so the bound above is generous to the gate. A gate that fails against a generous bound fails, which is the one direction of bias an unreachability argument can absorb. The same estimator would need a correction, not an appeal to direction, if the argument ran the other way — if a ceiling were being claimed as reachable — and no argument in this paper does that. scripts/record_stage1_claims.py refuses to record at all if the measured gain ever reaches the declared target, because that outcome would demand rewriting this section rather than re-rendering it, and tests/test_evaluation_population_bound.py supplies the passage that makes the refusal fire.

One derived quantity moves when the denominator is corrected, and the corrected one is the honest figure for a same-population statement. Against the training budget the agent captures 89.9% of the available first-order signal; against the bound on the passage it is actually scored on, 57.3%. The first compares a held-out numerator to a training denominator and is reported here only because the literature’s usual framing does the same.

The trained agent realizes 0.9229 nats, which is 89.9% of what the order allows (tbl. 19). Under the declared gate that near-optimal result reads as a failure, and the natural response to a failure — build a better bigram model — is guaranteed to be wasted. An unreachable gate does not merely fail to discriminate; it actively points the work in a direction that cannot succeed. The restated gate is the context-free unigram baseline, which the agent clears by 8.0343 perplexity units. That bar is reachable and, unlike uniform, diagnostic — with one qualification the ledger carries. A model can beat uniform while carrying no context at all, and beating the training-estimated unigram on a finite held-out passage is consistent with using the previous letter but does not by itself attribute the gain to it: a different context-free distribution can land below the count-estimated bar through distribution shift alone, and one measurably does — the trained transition’s own context-marginalized distribution scores 19.955 against the bar’s 19.9558 on this passage. The attribution is carried instead by a context-destruction control: rotating the trained conditionals off their own contexts — the same thirty distributions, mis-assigned — collapses the model to 159.3667, far above the bar on the identical positions, so the margin the agent realizes is attributable to correctly-assigned previous-letter conditioning rather than to the letter frequencies its transition happens to carry.

10.1.2 Stage 2: the declared threshold sat below the baseline, against an absent oracle

The Stage 2 gate was declared as letter->phoneme accuracy >=60% on the English EWT oracle. The first error is that the oracle does not exist. Universal Dependencies English EWT is a syntactic treebank (Nivre et al. 2020; Silveira et al. 2014); its CoNLL-U fields are lemma, upos, feats, and deprel, with no phonemic annotation of any kind. The line had been copied from the Stage 4 case gate, where UD is at least the right corpus — though sec. 4.6 shows the eight-way labeling that gate scores against is a documented heuristic rather than a gold standard, so it was defective too, for a different reason. A phoneme task cannot be scored on UD at all, at any threshold.

The second error survives fixing the first. Measured on held-out CMUdict, a context-free per-letter lookup table — no transition matrix, no pymdp, no active inference — scores 70.255%. The declared threshold sits below the trivial baseline, so a model doing nothing hierarchical passes. By eq. 12 the verdict is VACUOUS, and it would have remained vacuous on the correct corpus.

Table 22: Both shipped gate defects worked through eq. 12, with the measured baseline and comparator that classify them. Stage 1 and Stage 2B use held-out evaluation populations; Stage 2A is explicitly an in-sample full-dictionary protocol, and its baseline, model, and exact all-position bound share the same 800,198-position denominator. The Stage 2A row is the same unreachable wording inherited one level down, caught before it shipped by applying the check that Stage 1 had already forced. The comparator-type column is load-bearing and is stated rather than left to the reader. A model-class bound is an upper bound on what any model of the class can reach, so a threshold beyond it cannot be met by better engineering. A reference model is a measured system with information the shipped one forgoes; it can be exceeded, and at Stage 4 it is, so the taxonomy no longer permits UNREACHABLE against a reference at all — a reference failing the bar classifies ABOVE_REFERENCE, a statement about that comparator and not a theorem. One residual asymmetry is recorded rather than silently absorbed: when the stronger empirical comparator (a reference model fitted on more information, such as sec. 10.1.6’s lookup table) clears a bar the shipped model fails, ABOVE_REFERENCE still reads as a statement about the declared comparator. A future classifier revision could separate that case as a distinct verdict (REFERENCE_NOT_CLEARED: a stronger measured comparator cleared the bar and the shipped model did not) from the model-class-bound UNREACHABLE; that revision belongs to the gate code, not this manuscript, so the limitation is stated here. The two other types the project uses elsewhere are a privileged oracle (Stage 3’s held-out word model, Stage 5’s type oracle) and an analytic bound (generation’s zero distance). Calling all four a ceiling would license claiming more from a bracketed verdict than the comparator supports, which is why the type is an argument to the classifier rather than a caption.

The middle row of tbl. 22 is the payoff. Once Stage 1’s defect had been diagnosed as unreachable rather than as a threshold that happened to be wrong, the same measurement was cheap to repeat at Level 2, where the available gain over uniform is 0.9016 nats on the exact all-position protocol, below the inherited 2-nat threshold. The wording would have shipped a second time. A taxonomy earns its keep by making the second instance of a defect cheaper to find than the first.

10.1.3 A reproducible subsample is not a representative one

The third finding is not about the threshold but about what the threshold is evaluated on, and it is the one most likely to recur, because the reasoning that produces it is locally correct.

The letter-to-phone evaluation originally took a deterministic prefix of the held-out pair list, pairs[:limit], on the argument that a prefix needs no seed and is therefore perfectly reproducible. It is. But g2p_pairs is alphabetically sorted, so a prefix is only words from the start of the alphabet. Reproducibility and representativeness are independent properties, and satisfying the first is not evidence about the second. Measured on that prefix the letter-to-phone (G2P) margin is 1.691 points against the full set’s 0.546, an overstatement by a factor of 3.1, which reads as a comfortable pass rather than the thin one it is. The prefix spans 4 word initials where the full held-out set spans 27. Evenly spaced indices cost exactly the same and span far more of them, and _iter_pairs in src/ailm/levels/phoneme.py now takes a stride instead.

The finding is not asserted from those numbers, it is re-derived from them: scripts/record_subsample_claims.py computes the overstatement factor from the two recorded margins and refuses to record if it is not greater than one, and refuses again if the prefix ever spans as many initials as the full set. Either refusal means the bias this section is built on has disappeared and the section needs rewriting, which is the outcome a guard should force rather than absorb.

Fixing the bias exposes a second problem underneath it, and separating the two is the part worth generalizing. The first contrast is about selection and holds size fixed: the alphabetical prefix over 7982 positions against an evenly spaced stride truncated to the same size, 7959 positions, whose margin is 0.327 points — much nearer the full-set figure than the prefix’s. The second contrast is about size and holds selection fixed: that same honest stride returns p = 0.2375, and a denser stride, with a margin of 0.489 points, is closer but still short of the declared criterion, while the full 42,820 positions reach p = 3.468e-06. An unbiased subsample of the same size is underpowered. The biased prefix had looked significant, and it looked significant for the wrong reason: not because the effect was large but because the subset was easy. The bounded pymdp subsample the stage tests still run — 13,224 positions, p = 0.02881 — is kept for exactly that reason: it is a live demonstration that this procedure returns “not significant” on real data of an inadequate size.

At the Bonferroni-corrected per-test threshold of the declared family, 0.000625 (sec. 15.2), the full set has power 0.943796 against the fixed reference share 0.55 over its 2524 discordant pairs: it could have detected the smallest effect this project treats as interesting. Its effect size and exact interval are recorded with the remaining primary paired effects in tbl. 36.

fig. 28 shows why neither subsample is an acceptable evaluation. The resolution was not to shrink the claim or inflate the sample, but to remove the constraint that forced subsampling in the first place: test pymdp and the numpy oracle against each other on a bounded subset — 13,224 of the 42,820 held-out positions — where they disagree on 0 positions (eq. 16), then compute full-set statistics with the fast oracle. That is tested equivalence on the checked positions and an extrapolation beyond them, not a proof that the two decoders are the same function (sec. 4.11). The same bias recurred in Part A, where a length-matched-subset measurement gives 15.2882 for a quantity whose full-dictionary value is 16.7445; the two are different measurements over different position sets and must not be reported interchangeably, so Part A is now computed in closed form over all 800,198 positions.

10.1.4 Level 3: the declared gate states a condition the bar itself already clears

Level 3’s declared gate was “perplexity below 500 on PTB-1k”. Measured, the letter-bigram bar itself scores 9.0547, clearing 500 by a factor of 55.2. The gate was vacuous by a wide margin and named a corpus the project does not have — the third borrowed round constant to turn out to constrain nothing.

The restated gate compares the level against a letter-bigram model over the identical alphabet and the same whole-document training partition. The bar is fitted to every training type while the word prior is fitted to its bounded lexicon; both are scored on the identical held-out in-vocabulary positions. This gives the non-lexical comparator strictly broader training support. tbl. 23 places it against the full comparator ladder.

That reference is not a bound on every admissible model. Unlike Stage 2 the margin is wide by construction, so no paired test is needed — a measured conclusion, not an omission.

The margin is comfortable. That comfort is exactly what makes the level the sharpest illustration of the lesson tbl. 28 introduced one level down: a lexicon is so much information that almost any word prior beats a letter model. In all, five mis-wirings were built against the bar; four are scored and recorded, and tabulated below. The remaining arm — end-of-word emitted one position early — assigns zero probability to every true path, so its perplexity is unbounded and it is not a comparable number. It is reasoned rather than recorded (decision 14). Table 24: 3 of the 5 Level 3 mis-wirings clear the bar of 9.0547; the 4 with finite perplexity are shown. The third is the striking one: inverting the frequency ranking, so that the rarest words are predicted most confidently, still beats a letter-bigram model. Mis-wiring Per-emission perplexity Caught by the bar?
Uniform prior over words — lexicon kept, frequencies discarded 4.8095 no

What pins the level is not the bar but a closed-form identity. Because every factor except the word prior is deterministic, the probability the model assigns to a word’s whole emission path must equal that word’s unigram probability. A live pymdp walk and an independent derivation that imports neither pymdp nor jax agree to 1.12e-06 nats over 400 vocabulary words. All three surviving mis-wirings change the word prior, so every one fails it.

The general form of the lesson: when a level’s mechanism is highly informative, the baseline comparison stops discriminating precisely because the level is good. Necessary conditions get weaker as models get stronger, and a gate built only from them gets correspondingly less able to fail.

10.1.5 Level 4: one threshold failing in opposite directions on each population

Level 4’s declared gate was “at least 60 percent against the UD 8-case oracle”. It fails in both directions simultaneously, and which failure is observed depends only on which population the threshold is scored against. tbl. 25 scores it against both.

This is the clearest evidence in the project for a claim the earlier stages only gesture at: a threshold without a named population is not a threshold. The same number, the same corpus and the same model yield opposite verdicts, and nothing in the declared gate’s wording distinguishes them.

The restated Stage 4 gate is beating the context-free \(\arg\max\, p(\text{case} \mid \text{UPOS})\) bar on the derived population, defended by a paired test: 50.72% against 42.91%, a margin of 7.81 points over 1319 positions, with 205 against 102 discordant positions at \(p =\) 4.213e-09. No gate is stated on the gold population, for the reason sec. 4.6 measures: the committed split yields identical predictions from the fitted sequence model and its context-free comparator. That is an empirical paired null on this split, not an exact consequence of the constant observation. The model’s favored share of those 307 discordant positions is 0.667752, marginal exact 95% interval [0.612006, 0.720224], with power 0.04599 against the fixed reference share 0.55 at the family-corrected threshold (tbl. 36): unlike the Stage 2B comparison, this one could not have detected the smallest effect the project treats as interesting.

10.1.6 A context-free comparator is necessary but not sufficient

Requirement 1 of the staged-gate method (sec. 2) says the comparator is context-free and never uniform, because a model that beats uniform has shown only that it knows which symbols are frequent. That requirement is necessary. It is not sufficient, and this section is the demonstration, on this project’s own gates.

Nothing in those requirements or in the pre-build checklist says to look for the strongest comparator that is still not the model. So each gate was stated against the first defensible comparator rather than the best one. Searching that class instead of picking from it changes two verdicts’ meaning (tbl. 26).

The search is austere by design. For each level, fit an argmax over counts of (previous observed symbol, current observed symbol) to the label, on the training split alone, backing off to the per-symbol argmax where a pair is unseen. There is no latent state, no filtering, no inference at decode time, and strictly less information than the filtering decode uses, which sees the whole left context through its belief state. It is the obvious thing, which is the point: a comparator that took ingenuity to construct would be a weaker criticism than one that does not.

Table 26: The strongest member of the comparator class, searched rather than assumed. The declared-context-free-bar row is the shipped bar, recomputed by this probe and required to reproduce it; that agreement is what establishes the probe scores the gate’s own population rather than a similar one.
Stage 2B letter-to-phone Level 4 case
declared context-free bar 70.2546% 42.9113%
shipped model 70.801% 50.72%
left-context lookup 72.8188% 55.4208%
lookup parameters 677 65
lookup over model 2.0177 pts 4.7005 pts
model’s own margin 0.546 pts 7.81 pts

At Stage 2B the lookup exceeds the shipped model by 2.0177 points, which is several times the model’s entire recorded margin over its declared bar. At Level 4 it exceeds it by 4.7005.

No recorded number is withdrawn. The model accuracies, the context-free bars, the margins and every gate verdict stand exactly as recorded, and all of them reproduce. What is withdrawn is an interpretation: that clearing the declared bar showed the latent-state machinery doing the work. It did not, because the bar was not the hardest thing in its own class.

The controls, including the one that is weak. A positive control requires the bigram lookup not to score below the per-symbol argmax it backs off to, since it uses strictly more context; it does not at either level. A negative control deranges the same map, holding the key set, the label multiset and the parameter count fixed and changing only which label sits at which key. At Stage 2B that collapses to 0.6913%, which is clean. At Level 4 it reaches 47.4602%, above the bar and below the lookup, so a substantial share of the Level 4 result is context-conditional label frequency rather than the specific mapping. That is reported rather than suppressed, and it means the Level 4 half of this finding should be discounted relative to the Stage 2B half.

Why this belongs in the paper rather than in a reviewer’s report. It is the gate-audit defect class recurring inside the repair, found by applying the project’s own discipline to the project’s own method. The taxonomy of eq. 12 is unaffected: a verdict still classifies a threshold against a baseline and a typed comparator, and those verdicts are still right. What this shows is that the check is not yet a procedure. A procedure would say: enumerate the comparator class, fit its strongest member on training data alone, and place the threshold above that. Requirement 1 asks only that the comparator not be uniform, and the distance between those two demands is the distance between a taxonomy and a method.

This is the sharpest available argument that the working hypothesis of sec. 2 is worth testing outside this repository. A check that its own author can defeat by fitting a two-symbol lookup table is a check whose failure modes are not yet exhausted.

10.2 Executable gate-audit report

Both defects were found by hand, and being found by hand is not a property that survives contact with a schedule. scripts/audit_gates.py performs the classification of eq. 12 as an executable artifact: for each implemented stage it measures the trivial baseline, the shipped model, and the typed comparator and prints them together. Its inventory comprises the rows of tbl. 22, the implemented later-stage rows of tbl. 27, and the generation gate, whose comparators belong with the rest of that level and are tabulated in sec. 4.9. The inventory is fixed by AUDITED_GATE_IDS in src/ailm/gates.py and compared, in order, against the rows the script actually built; a mismatch aborts the run with its own exit code before a single verdict is printed. A gate that quietly stopped being audited therefore fails the run rather than vanishing from it, which is the failure mode an audit script is most prone to and least able to notice.

The script exits non-zero if any ordinary verdict is not bracketed (of either strength) or if the model sits on the wrong side of its own bar, with one exception required by the outcome of the retained case-only clause ablation (sec. 4.7). That row must remain ABOVE_REFERENCE, both the model and fitted privileged reference must sit on the failing side, both whole-document-bootstrap privileged-label intervals must span zero, and the planted-effect control must fire. A model pass, a comparator that clears the bar, or a resolved interval trips the exit code, because any of them means the finding changed rather than that the status string may remain fixed. Stages with no implementation are printed as UNAUDITED alongside their declared thresholds, so an unchecked gate is visible rather than absent.

Three properties of the audit bound what a clean run establishes. The typed comparators include a smoothing decode, a conditional entropy, a per-item argmax, an oracle given the answer — and only some of them bound the model class. The verdict carries that distinction rather than leaving it to a footnote: each row declares its comparator’s type, BRACKETED_BOUND and BRACKETED_REFERENCE say which strength of comparator beat the baseline, and a reference clearing a bar never reads as a bound doing so. Where the shipped model scores above its own recorded smoothing reference, as on the Stage 4 derived row, the script prints the row with an explicit warning rather than reclassifying it, because the row is still bracketed-by-reference. The audit classifies placement only: it says nothing about whether a margin is large enough to be believed, which is the separate question sec. 15.2 answers and which no threshold comparison can answer on its own.

The third property is the one this section’s own history creates. Almost every threshold the script audits is a restated threshold, restated after its stage had been built and measured — the audit sets each row’s bar to the measured baseline of the population the model is then scored against. A clean run therefore certifies that the restated rows are placed where the audit convention places them; it does not certify that any of them was chosen without knowledge of the answer. That is retrospective re-certification rather than sequential validation, and sec. 15.2 states what it costs every significance verdict downstream. The counterweight is that a restated gate can still fail: the retained case-only clause row is restated exactly like the others and the shipped model lands on its failing side. Its fitted privileged reference now does too, and its gain remains unresolved under whole-document resampling (sec. 4.7), which is why the script treats a model pass or an interval that no longer spans zero as an alarm.

The canonical Stage 5 row is the one exception to the restatement, and it is worth stating plainly rather than leaving a reader to infer it from a date. Its bar was written down in the decision record before the artifact it scores was regenerated, together with the alphabet, the population, the comparators, the controls, the predictions and the falsifiers, and the entry said in as many words that a mixture failing that bar would mean the widening was decorative. The mixture cleared it. That is a stronger claim about placement than any restated row here can make, and a weaker one than the confirmatory replication of sec. 10.6, because registration and outcome share one development session and no held-back partition survives on which to repeat it (sec. 5.7.3).

The quoted speech threshold uses text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis.

10.3 Pre-build gate requirements

Applied before writing the level, not after measuring it. Steps 1 through 4 are cheap — they need the corpus, not the model. No gate in this project was built this way: each was declared cheaply, found defective once measured, and restated against the measurement. The checklist is what that experience recommends, not what it records.

  1. Name the metric and its direction. Fix which side of the threshold is passing, in code, before any number exists. eq. 10 is where a sign error becomes a silently inverted gate.
  2. Measure the trivial baseline \(b_P\). Build the dumbest model that produces a number on this task — context-free frequencies, a per-item lookup table, the majority class — and score it on the real evaluation set. If \(b_P \succ t\), the gate is vacuous on that population; restate it against \(b_P\) and stop.
  3. Measure and type the comparator \(c_P\), on the evaluation population. Use the conditional entropy of that population, an oracle with access the model does not have, or another explicit reference, and declare which comparator type the taxonomy assigns it. If \(c_P \nsucc t\), a bound type makes the gate UNREACHABLE; an exceedable type makes it ABOVE_REFERENCE and licenses no impossibility claim. A training-distribution entropy is a legitimate calibration reference and is not \(c_P\) for a gate scored held-out; if it is all that is available, say so in the row and do not read the verdict as a same-population comparison. Never inherit a threshold constant from another stage without redoing this step — that is precisely how the 2-nat wording reached Level 2. classify_gate refuses an untyped comparator, and only a bound type can produce “no implementation could pass”.
  4. Confirm \(b_P\) and \(c_P\) were measured on the same population \(P\) the gate scores the model on. A comparator from one subset and a baseline from another produce a margin that describes nothing, and eq. 12 is a function of the pair \((t, P)\) — a verdict quoted without its population is not a verdict.
  5. Check the evaluation set for structural bias. Is it sorted? Is a prefix a proper subset of some category? Is it length-, frequency-, or alphabetically filtered? Reproducible is not representative.
  6. Check the evaluation set for power at the corrected threshold. If the expected margin is small, compute whether the intended sample size can establish it at all — against the family-corrected per-test threshold of sec. 15.2, not the nominal one, because adding a test tightens the bar for every test. With an exact test the question has a sharper form than “is power adequate”: below a minimum discordant count there is no rejection region at any outcome, and exact_two_sided_rejection_region returns that emptiness rather than a small number. An honest effect on an underpowered sample fails, and that failure is uninformative.
  7. Write the negative control before the model. A deliberately broken variant — transposed matrix, uniform emission, shuffled labels — that must land on the failing side. If it passes, GateVacuousError and the stage is blocked (sec. 4.11).
  8. Check that the failure signature is sufficient, not merely necessary. tbl. 28 is the counterexample: the wrong-normalization mis-wiring cleared the baseline bar while being wrong. Add an invariant that pins the structure directly.
  9. Record every threshold, baseline, and typed comparator in the ledger and register the gate in AUDITED_GATE_IDS and scripts/audit_gates.py, so the classification is re-derived on every run rather than remembered and a gate that stops being audited fails the run.
  10. Declare any new inferential p-value into the multiplicity family. A threshold-crossing claim that is not a member of SIGNIFICANCE_FAMILY is judged against an uncorrected threshold while tightening nobody else’s, which is the one way to add a test and make every existing claim look stronger. A descriptive diagnostic or re-analysis may remain outside only through a named, machine-checked exclusion and prose that carries no threshold-crossing inference (sec. 15.2).
  11. Fix the threshold and the test before the population is scored, and hold a partition back for them. A gate restated after its stage has been measured, or a p-value declared into the family once its value is known, is retrospective re-certification: the correction of sec. 15.2 bounds a fixed family’s Type-I rate and does nothing about a test chosen with the answer already in view. Step 2 and step 3 are the steps that consume the evaluation set, so the partition the final gate is scored on must be one they never touched.

10.4 Level 3: the letter-bigram bar admits a wrong word prior

10.4.1 The letter-bigram bar does not catch a wrong word prior

The level also relocates where the learned content sits. At the letter and phoneme levels the corpus statistics parameterize the transition; here both transitions are structural constants and the single learned quantity is the prior over word identity. That is the level’s whole content — a lexicon with frequencies — and it moves the mis-wiring risk with it. A wrong prior at Level 3 is what a wrong transition was at Level 1, with one difference that sec. 10.1.4 makes the case for: the letter-bigram bar does not catch it. fig. 29 shows the four finite-score mis-wirings beside the correct construction, and which of them the bar catches.

10.4.2 The closed form scales to every length-eligible training type

The vocabulary bound is a property of the agent, not of the model, and the two scale differently. Because every factor except the word prior is deterministic, the closed form is exact at any vocabulary size — a word’s score simply is its prior mass — so the model can be measured wherever a lexicon can be built.

Measured over all 38,007 Brown training types that meet the word-length eligibility rule, coverage rises to 96.74% of held-out tokens and the level scores 3.6062 per emission against a letter-bigram bar of 10.1266 over 548,866 emissions.

Numeric coverage and per-emission perplexity both rise, but their utility directions oppose: more coverage is desirable and more perplexity is worse. So the level is measured at 8 nested frequency-ranked lexicon sizes rather than at two endpoints (fig. 30).

Reading that ladder correctly requires two cautions, and both cut against the easy version of the result.

The comparator is not re-fit at each rung. It is estimated once from the full training frequencies and re-scored on whatever tokens each rung’s lexicon covers, so its matrices are bit-identical at every rung and all of its movement is the changing evaluation population rather than a changing model. That population is the second caution: a rung scores only the held-out tokens its lexicon can represent, because the model assigns no mass outside its vocabulary, so a smaller lexicon is scored on a smaller and more frequent — that is, easier — subset of the same stream. Perplexity is an average over that subset, which makes the per-emission gain incomparable across rungs by construction.

Both numbers are therefore recorded. Per emission the gain is nearly flat, from 0.9638 to 1.0325 nats, and slightly non-monotone. Weighted so that every rung shares the top rung’s denominator — the same one-denominator rule the coverage axis already follows — the gain widens strictly and by 111.49%, from 0.4882 to 1.0325. The shared-denominator series is the one that compares rungs; the per-emission series is what a reader of the table at a single operating point sees. Quoting only the per-emission series would report a property of the denominator as a property of the model, which is the error this level’s own coverage rule exists to prevent.

The tempting reading, that the margin narrows because a larger lexicon is a harder problem, is an artifact of comparing per-emission means over moving populations. On the shared denominator, the gain widens across every rung.

The gate stays bracketed at every rung: no rung has the comparator at or below the model.

The pymdp agent does not follow it there. The word factor’s dense transition would be 5.78 GB at float32, so instantiation caps at roughly 17,320 types, and the builder raises with that arithmetic rather than failing on an allocation. Stating which of the two capabilities is lost above the cap — the ability to run pymdp, not the ability to measure the model — is the point of enforcing the bound explicitly. A custom lexicon can be substituted for the frequency-ranked one, in which case evaluation still uses held-out running text restricted to what that lexicon covers, never the lexicon scored against itself.

A comparison the reader must not make: the perplexities in this section are per emission over 27 symbols — 26 letters plus an end-of-word marker — while Level 1’s are over 30 running-text symbols including space and punctuation. They are different quantities over different alphabets and different position sets, and placing them in one table would be a category error. N_OBS and N_SYMBOLS are asserted to differ so that the warning is enforced rather than remembered.

10.5 Beating the context-free baseline is necessary, not sufficient

Level 1 established that a mis-wired emission is detectable numerically but not structurally. Level 2 sharpens the lesson, because its emission and transition are both learned and expose separate placements for the error, and because one of the mis-wirings tested against it passed the signature that caught the first one.

Table 28: The listed mis-wirings are evaluated against the same context-free baseline on the same deterministic stride subsample. The wrong-normalization row clears the baseline while being wrong, so the baseline signature is necessary but not sufficient.
Mis-wiring Caught by “beats the context-free baseline”? What does catch it
Time-reversed B, i.e. \(P(\text{prev} \mid \text{cur})\) yes — falls below the bar the baseline comparison, and an index assertion on B[0, next, current, 0]
Uniform, information-free A yes — collapses far below the bar the baseline comparison
A normalized over phones instead of letters, then renormalized so pymdp still validates it no — clears the bar while wrong column sums of A[0, :, p] checked before any renormalization, and a value-for-value comparison of the shipped emission against an independent numpy re-derivation

The third row in tbl. 28 is the useful one. An emission normalized along the wrong axis and then renormalized is column-stochastic, so pymdp._validate() accepts it; it is also close enough to the correct emission that a filtering decode still beats a lookup table. Every check of the form “the model beats the trivial comparator” would pass. Two invariants pin the emission, and they catch the mis-wiring at different moments. The first is that A[0, :, p] sums to one over letters for each phone \(p\) — but only before renormalization, because renormalizing is exactly what restores that sum, and the guard is paired with a control asserting that the phone-normalized matrix does break it. The second catches the renormalized variant, where the first cannot: the shipped emission is compared value-for-value against an independent numpy re-derivation of \(P(\text{letter} \mid \text{phone})\), and that comparison carries its own non-vacuity assertion — the mis-normalized matrix must differ from the correct one by more than the comparison’s tolerance, or value equality would not be able to see it either. Structural validation and comparator-beating are both necessary; neither is sufficient, and only a value-level comparison against an independent derivation is sensitive to the difference between a right answer and a nearly right one.

10.6 Held-back replication of eligible family members

The sixteen-member significance family was assembled retrospectively, on the population every gate was revised against, and no correction factor turns that into confirmation. The family is frozen and this section does not reopen it. Its clause-level member is the case-only arm’s paired classification test, which is the arm that was scored when the family was frozen; promoting the widened arm to canonical does not move that member, rename it, or add one. The members with a genuine held-back partition available were the four computed on EWT populations: the UD English EWT test split, which no script in this repository had scored. Under the protocol of sec. 4.12, registered as decision 111 in the decisions log, those four were scored against it exactly once. The population is the whole of that split, 2077 sentences and 25,094 tokens across 316 authenticated source documents, vendored through the identical generators, oracles, exclusion rules and minimum-length filters, with no stride applied because nothing is fitted on it. Every model parameter was read unchanged from the existing development train fits, and the recorder refused to run unless the arrays it built were equal, element for element, to the ones the development artifacts produce. The document identities are disjoint from every development document identity. Both controls were run on this same population before any member was scored: the planted-effect positive control fired decisively (1131 against 448 discordant pairs, p = 3.525e-68), and the label-shuffled negative control did not (445 against 490, p = 0.1501), so a null on this population is a measurement rather than an instrument failure. Of the 4 members scored, two cross the frozen per-test threshold of 0.000625 in the direction their development result recorded, and two yield no discordant pair at all and are therefore not shown rather than shown absent (tbl. 29). Every registered direction and threshold prediction held. The remaining 12 members of the frozen family were not rescored and remain development-population inference. The controls, paired counts, and document-clustered intervals are shown together in fig. 31. The run cannot be repeated: the sentinel claim marks the population spent, and the recorder refuses a second pass.
